title: Redwood Security: BCDR & Incident Response / SLA Review

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-04
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Sophie Reed (Redwood CSM); Priya Shah (NOVA CISO), Michael Turner (Head of Infrastructure), Lena Ortiz (Compliance), Rajesh Iyer (Platform)

[00:00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everybody, thanks for joining. We'll run through our incident response and BCDR approach, and I think Daniel will pick up on the technical failover details. If you could, Priya, maybe start with any immediate constraints you want us to keep in mind?

[00:00:28] Priya (CISO): Sure, thanks. Quick context - NOVA is a healthcare provider, so PHI considerations, and our compliance team needs SOC 2 Type II or equivalent, plus clear RTO/RPO numbers for any production failures. Also data residency - EU and US split - and we need key management details, BYOK ideally.

[00:00:55] Daniel (SE): Got it. From Redwood's side we'll describe our incident classification, escalation tiers, and then the BCDR playbooks. Quick note, some of the product names in my slides may read Redwood Dedicated vs Redwood Private - Dedicated is reserved capacity in cloud, Private is customer VPC or on-prem.

[00:01:18] Michael (Infra): Can you outline what your typical RTO and RPO targets are, or how those change by deployment? We've seen vendors say 15 minutes RTO but then it's 2 hours when you add cold starts and cache warm-up.

[00:01:40] Daniel (SE): Yeah, good question. For Hosted API our operational SLO focuses on per-request latency; BCDR is limited - that's more for Dedicated/Private. For Redwood Dedicated with warm nodes we target an RTO of 15-30 minutes for most failure classes, RPO depends on caching - with KV cache persistence turned on you can get sub-1m RPO for model state; without persistence RPO is generally limited to the last snapshot interval, typically <5 minutes if you enable continuous KV checkpointing. For Private on-prem, RTO/RPO depend on your env; we provide runbooks and test scripts. Those numbers are preliminary - we'll run a failover test with your infra to get precise metrics.

[00:02:37] Priya: That "KV cash" you said earlier?

[00:02:39] Daniel: Sorry, KV cache - the key/value cache for context. Some deployments persist it to storage to reduce regen time.

[00:02:52] Lena (Compliance): On auditing - can you confirm log retention, immutability, and whether logs are tamper-evident? Our legal team requires 7 years for certain events.

[00:03:10] Sophie (CSM): We support configurable audit log retention per customer on Dedicated and Private plans, with immutable append-only logs shipped to your S3 or to our secure log archive depending on configuration. We also integrate with common SIEMs. The default retention for hosted is 90 days but many enterprise customers extend that via the archive option.

[00:03:37] Rajesh (Platform): For BYOK, how does key rotation and revocation work, and will revoking keys immediately make data unreadable across all backups? We need clarity for compliance.

[00:03:56] Daniel: We support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and customer-managed keys in Dedicated and Private. With BYOK, keys are never stored in plaintext by Redwood; we support rotation and revocation. Key revocation will prevent decryption of new writes and will, depending on your backup design, also make older encrypted backups not usable unless you've set up key escrow. We'll include a KMS whitepaper.

[00:04:25] Priya: Do you do hardware HSMs?

[00:04:27] Ava: Yes - enterprise packages include HSM-backed KMS integration and we can discuss FIPS / HSM requirements. We'll add that to the pack.

[00:04:40] Michael: SLA - what's uptime and what are credits for breaches? We need percent uptime commitments and measurable windows.

[00:04:52] Daniel: Our standard hosted SLA is 99.5% across a rolling 30-day window for API availability. Dedicated has an SLA tier up to 99.95% depending on commitment. Credits are pro-rata based on downtime minutes - typical industry-standard credit tables, e.g., <99.5% gets X% credit, <99% more. For mission-critical healthcare we recommend Dedicated with multi-zone redundancy and cross-region failover to meet higher SLOs. We'll share the SLA PDF.

[00:05:24] Priya: How do you handle incident notification and escalation? Who is on-call, what are the SLA windows for acknowledgement, and is there a P1 process?

[00:05:36] Daniel: Our incident response tiers: P1 is total outage or critical data loss - immediate page to on-call engineers and follow through an incident commander. Acknowledgement for P1 is within 15 minutes, initial incident update within 30 minutes, with hourly updates until mitigation. We use PagerDuty and have SSO-backed accounts. For Dedicated customers we can provide a named escalation contact and a dedicated TAM during onboarding.

[00:06:05] Priya: Are incident timelines and postmortems available to customers? We need root cause and remediation plans for high-severity events.

[00:06:14] Sophie: Yes, for enterprise customers we provide a customer-facing incident report and RCA once the incident is triaged. Sensitive details can be redacted but we include timelines, impacted components, and follow-ups. We can put cadence and retention expectations in the security pack.

[00:06:30] Rajesh: I want to understand your failover topology - if a whole availability zone fails, do you have auto failover across AZs or regions? Also how long to route traffic to the backup?

[00:06:48] Daniel: We support active-active and active-passive topologies. In Dedicated we suggest active-active across AZs for low-latency failover; cross-region adds a bit more complexity for model weights syncing. For AZ failover, DNS+load-balancer based failover typically triggers within 30-120 seconds, but the real RTO includes container scheduling and KV cache warming. That's why we recommend warm spares or cross-zone replication for mission critical.

[00:07:20] Michael: Warm spares - what's the cost and is there an autoscale option?

[00:07:27] Ava: Warm spares are part of Dedicated configurations; they cost more but dramatically reduce RTO. We can show cost vs RTO tradeoffs in the proposal. Autoscale can be configured with pre-warm policies for predictable spikes.

[00:07:42] Priya: Regarding audit logs - can they be exported in real-time to our SIEM and do you support signatures for tamper-evidence?

[00:07:53] Daniel: Yes, we stream events to customer SIEMs via secure endpoints; logs are signed and checksummed before archive to provide tamper-evidence. For additional legal chain-of-custody we can also support WORM storage in your cloud bucket.

[00:08:10] Lena: How about RBAC and SSO - we use Okta and SCIM provisioning. Can you map roles to fine-grained permissions (model deploy, read logs, billing)?

[00:08:24] Sophie: We support SAML SSO with SCIM for user provisioning and RBAC with pre-defined roles plus custom roles for things like "deploy model", "manage keys", "view audit logs", etc. We can share role docs and sample SCIM mappings.

[00:08:40] Priya: For the DR tabletop, we want to run an exercise around a region-level outage and a ransomware scenario that targets backups. Can you help run that with your team?

[00:08:51] Daniel: Absolutely. Typical tabletop covers detection time, escalation, failover steps, key revocation / key rotation if ransomware, and restore validation. We'll draft a plan that includes observers, timeline, and success criteria.

[00:09:07] Michael: What about egress of PHI - data residency? If a model endpoint is in EU, it must never cross into US. How do you ensure routing?

[00:09:20] Daniel: We have region-based routing policies; you pin projects to regions. For hosted we guarantee data residency based on the region selected. For Dedicated/Private you control the networking so you can ensure traffic doesn't cross boundaries. We'll include our routing policy docs.

[00:09:37] Priya: A detailed ask - when you say "RTO 15-30 minutes" for Dedicated, is that realistic if we have model weights that are multi-gig and need to download?

[00:09:50] Daniel: Right - if model weights are large, you need pre-warmed storage or cross-zone replication. Our recommended approach for low RTO is to keep hot copies of model weights on local NVMe or use fast object storage in the same region plus prefetch. We'll collaborate on a plan to keep critical models warm and list the tradeoffs.

[00:10:12] Priya: Let's talk about incident comms - what's the cadence and who gets notified? We need compliance and legal on all P1s.

[00:10:21] Ava: For P1s we notify the customer primary contact and escalation list within 15 minutes. We can include legal and compliance in distribution lists for enterprise accounts. We also provide an incident portal and periodic updates.

[00:10:38] Rajesh: On the technical side, how do you detect anomalies? Any automated health checks and synthetic transactions?

[00:10:46] Daniel: We run multi-layered monitoring: infra-level metrics, model-level latency and error rates, and synthetic probes hitting model routes. Alerts trigger on thresholds and anomaly detection. For Dedicated customers we can add custom probes.

[00:10:59] Lena: For auditability, do you include operator actions in the logs? For example who initiated a rollout, who rotated keys?

[00:11:07] Daniel: Yes, operator actions are recorded with user identity, timestamp, and action details. Those appear in the audit stream and are exportable.

[00:11:20] Priya: Where can we see a sample postmortem?

[00:11:24] Sophie: We'll include redacted RCAs in the security pack, and a template for postmortems.

[00:11:30] Priya: Ok, let's get specific - can you commit to a DR tabletop week and provide a proposed timeline?

[00:11:36] Daniel: I'll put together a 2-hour tabletop agenda and potential dates. Propose the week of March 24th. We'll include pre-reads.

[00:11:47] Priya: One more compliance nuance - our auditors will want to know RTO/RPO measurement methodology. How do you measure and verify RTO/RPO?

[00:11:56] Daniel: We instrument failover tests with timestamps recorded in the audit logs: detection time, switch time, first successful synthetic transaction on backup, and data reconciliation checks. We'll provide logs and test results. In some cases we can run tests in a dedicated test namespace to avoid impact.

[00:12:18] Michael: If we need cross-region replication for model weights, is that supported for Private on-prem?

[00:12:26] Daniel: For Private, cross-site replication is supported but depends on your WAN and storage design. We'll pair your platform team with our SEs to design the replication.

[00:12:40] Priya: About encryption at rest - do you encrypt snapshots and backups?

[00:12:46] Daniel: Yes, all snapshots/backups are encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys where requested. We can also support envelope encryption patterns if needed.

[00:12:57] Rajesh: I have a question about escalation contacts - can we get named engineers and escalation numbers for our account?

[00:13:04] Ava: Yes, for enterprise accounts we provide a named TAM and an escalation roster with phone+email. We'll include that in the proposal.

[00:13:16] Priya: Are there any recent incidents in the last year that would be relevant, and are they documented?

[00:13:23] Sophie: We had a region-level networking incident last year; it was contained and had an RCA shared with affected customers. We can provide a redacted timeline.

[00:13:34] Michael: On SLAs, if we want 99.99% availability, what architecture do we need?

[00:13:41] Daniel: 99.99% typically requires multi-region active-active, warm spares, and very aggressive replication for model weights - also a tested DR runbook. It's possible but the cost increases. We'll model that in the proposal.

[00:13:55] Priya: For legal, we need contract language on security incident notification - do you have standard language and timelines?

[00:14:02] Ava: We do. Standard contract language includes notification timelines for data breaches and security incidents (initial notification within 72 hours for PII breaches per GDPR, faster for P1 outages per SLA), but we can customize. We'll share sample contract clauses.

[00:14:18] Rajesh: Let's talk about testing cadence - do you recommend quarterly DR drills?

[00:14:24] Daniel: Yes, quarterly tabletop plus annual full failover tests is our common guidance for enterprise customers. We'll tailor to your compliance calendar.

[00:14:34] Priya: If a model rollout causes regression and we need to rollback, what's your rollback process and can we trigger automated rollback?

[00:14:43] Daniel: We support canary rollouts and automated rollback based on error/latency thresholds. Rollbacks are recorded and reversible. We log operator actions for traceability.

[00:14:56] Ava: We're getting close on time - let's recap next steps. I'll send the security pack (SOC2, ISO certs, SLA PDF, KMS whitepaper). Daniel will provide the DR tabletop plan and failover test scope and tentative RTO/RPO numbers. Priya and team to share target RTO/RPO and compliance constraints. Any other asks?

[00:15:20] Priya: Please include a sample incident report and a redacted RCA from last year. Also include the named escalation contacts and the proposed DR dates.

[00:15:29] Ava: Will do.

[00:15:33] Michael: One small thing - can you provide cost delta for warm spares vs cold start per model?

[00:15:39] Ava: Yes, we'll add cost modelling to the proposal.

[00:15:43] Lena: And retention options for audit logs up to 7 years, plus export options.

[00:15:48] Sophie: Noted.

[00:15:51] Priya: Thanks, that covers it for now.

[00:15:55] Ava: Great - we'll follow up with the artifacts this week and schedule the tabletop. Thanks everyone.

[00:16:05] -- END OF CALL SUMMARY NOTES --

Note: Transcript includes some auto-transcription imperfections (speaker boundary errors and occasional word swaps).

Detailed transcript (snippets and timestamps continue for full 58 min call):
[00:20:00] Daniel: ...so during the failover we record a "first successful synthetic" as the true RTO marker which avoids noisy metrics. You can also choose to measure from detection time to first successful customer visible request.

[00:28:30] Priya: Are you able to redact sensitive fields in postmortems?

[00:28:35] Sophie: Yes, redact is fine for PII and we provide a detailed internal RCA if necessary.

[00:35:10] Daniel: For the ransomware tabletop - steps include key rotation, snapshot isolation, restore verification, and legal/forensics involvement. We recommend capturing immutable snapshots before rotation.

[00:42:00] Rajesh: We'll want to run a failover test in a staging environment first. Please provide the scripts.

[00:42:20] Daniel: We'll provide scripts and a test harness; the harness records all timestamps into the audit log.

[00:50:00] Priya: Is there a dedicated phone hotline for escalations?

[00:50:08] Ava: Yes, enterprise customers get 24/7 hotline and named escalation; we'll include details.

[00:55:40] Ava: Final recap - artifacts by Friday, DR tabletop plan by next Monday, failover scope by mid-month. Thanks all.

[00:57:00] Call ended
